title: Distribution transformer failures
description: Distribution transformers fail from overheating, overloading, oil degradation, oil theft and poor earthing. Failures are expensive and cause long outages, so utilities need early warning of developing faults.

title: Faults and remote switching on power lines and substations
description: When a fault occurs on a line or substation, crews often patrol long distances to find it and switch by hand. Remote monitoring, fault location and remote switching shorten outages.

title: Customers unaware of power outages
description: Consumers and utilities often learn about outages late. Automatic outage alerts improve response times and customer communication.

title: Managing limited power with load shedding and prioritisation
description: When supply or backup capacity is limited, essential loads must keep running while non-critical loads are shed. Doing this manually is slow and error-prone.

title: Poor power quality: power factor, harmonics and voltage problems
description: Low power factor, harmonics, voltage sags, phase imbalance and wrong phase sequence waste energy, raise bills and damage equipment, especially in industry.

title: Fair, accurate electricity metering and billing
description: Shared meters in multi-tenant buildings, tampering, credit management and unclear consumption make electricity billing unfair or inaccurate.

title: Reliable backup power and source switching
description: Grid interruptions force switching between grid, generator, solar and batteries. Slow or unsafe changeover disrupts sensitive loads such as hospitals and data centres.

title: Fuel losses: consumption, theft, leakage and contamination
description: Generator sites, fuel stations and transport fleets lose money through inefficient running, theft, leaks and contaminated fuel.

title: Efficient power conversion for solar, batteries and drives
description: Solar systems, batteries, motors and chargers depend on inverters and converters. Their efficiency, protection and control determine how well the whole system performs.

title: Charging and managing electric vehicles
description: Electric bikes, tricycles and cars are growing in Tanzania, but charging infrastructure, battery management and charging billing are still limited.

title: Electrical installation safety
description: Faulty wiring, fake cables, poor earthing, lightning surges and unsafe maintenance cause shocks, fires and equipment damage.

title: Equipment and motor breakdowns
description: Motors and industrial equipment fail from overload, vibration, overheating and phase problems. Without condition monitoring and planned maintenance, breakdowns cause costly downtime.

title: Bringing electricity to unserved villages, islands and schools
description: Many villages, islands and rural institutions are far from the national grid. Extending lines, building mini-grids or using local generation each has different costs and technical limits.

title: Planning and operating grids as demand and renewables grow
description: Utilities must decide where to add generation, how to dispatch it cheaply and how to keep voltage and frequency stable as demand rises and more solar and wind connect. Forecasting, optimisation and better monitoring help them plan and run the grid reliably.

title: Safe, affordable buildings for growing towns
description: Schools, hostels, offices, hospitals and homes in fast-growing towns need multi-storey buildings that are safe, economical and built to code. Poor design and ageing structures lead to defects, costly repairs and collapse risk.

title: Bridges and safe crossings over rivers and roads
description: Rivers, valleys and busy roads cut communities off from markets, schools and hospitals, especially in the rainy season. Durable, affordable bridges and pedestrian crossings keep people and goods moving safely.

title: Costly or poor-quality building materials
description: Cement, sand and aggregates are expensive and their quality varies by source, which weakens concrete, blocks and bricks. Local and waste materials can cut cost and environmental impact if their strength and durability are proven.

title: Weak and expansive soils under roads and buildings
description: Black cotton and other expansive or weak soils swell, shrink and lose strength when wet, cracking roads and foundations. Stabilising them cheaply, often with local or waste materials, extends the life of what is built on them.

title: Roads that fail early and cost too much to maintain
description: Many roads rut, crack and pothole long before their design life because of poor materials, drainage and heavy loads. Better pavement design, materials and maintenance planning lower the cost of keeping roads usable.

title: Traffic congestion and unsafe junctions in cities
description: Growing cities face long queues at junctions, poor parking and mixed traffic that slows buses and endangers pedestrians. Better junction design, signals, parking and public transport priority keep traffic moving safely.

title: Water scarcity and unreliable supply
description: Villages, schools and fast-growing towns often lack a reliable water source, and supply networks lose much of what they carry. Harvesting rainwater, finding groundwater and designing efficient supply systems close the gap.

title: Flooding and poor storm water drainage
description: Heavy rain overwhelms blocked or undersized drains, flooding streets, homes and roads. Hydraulic modelling and well-designed drainage and flood control structures reduce damage and disease.

title: Construction projects that run late and over budget
description: Building and road projects often finish late, cost more than planned or are abandoned, because of late payments, poor planning, rework and skill shortages. Better project, cost and quality management protects public money.

title: High and invisible energy consumption
description: Homes, offices and facilities rarely see where their energy goes. Monitoring and automatic control help reduce waste and cost.

title: Energy access from renewable and waste sources
description: Off-grid and unreliable-grid areas need affordable local generation. Solar, wind, hydro, biomass and energy harvesting can supply or supplement power.

title: Faulty and wasteful street lighting
description: Street lights fail unnoticed or stay on unnecessarily, which reduces road safety and wastes energy.

title: Unsafe drinking and process water
description: Contaminated, salty or hard water harms health and equipment. Affordable monitoring and treatment are needed where laboratory testing is far away.

title: Water supply, pumping and leakage
description: Utilities and buildings struggle with burst pipes, overflowing tanks, unreliable supply and inefficient pumping, which wastes water and energy.

title: Water metering and billing
description: Shared connections and inaccurate meters make water billing unfair, and air in pipes can make meters read wrongly.

title: Inefficient irrigation water use
description: Manual irrigation wastes water and labour and gives crops uneven moisture. Automatic, sensor-driven and solar-powered irrigation can improve yields.

title: Sanitation, sewage and wastewater
description: Overflowing septic tanks, poor toilet hygiene and wasted grey water create health risks and lost resources.

title: Post-harvest losses: drying and storage
description: Crops, fish and fruit spoil quickly without good drying, cooling and storage. Smallholders lose a large share of their harvest after it leaves the field.

title: Livestock, poultry and aquaculture management
description: Poultry, fish and bee farmers need stable temperature, humidity, water quality and disease control. Manual care is labour-intensive and losses are high.

title: Protecting crops, stores and homes from pests and animals
description: Rodents, insects, mosquitoes, birds of prey and wild animals destroy crops and stores and spread disease.

title: Soil fertility and crop monitoring
description: Farmers often apply fertiliser and plant without knowing soil nutrients, moisture or growing conditions, which lowers yields and wastes inputs.

title: Mechanising small-scale food processing
description: Peeling, roasting, milling, sorting and cutting are often done by hand, which is slow, inconsistent and unhygienic.

title: Patient monitoring and medication adherence
description: Understaffed facilities and home-based patients need help with vital-sign monitoring, medication reminders and safe handling of samples and medicines.

title: Independence for people with disabilities
description: People with visual, hearing, speech or mobility impairments face barriers in moving, communicating and voting independently.

title: Road accidents and driver behaviour
description: Speeding, drunk or drowsy driving, glare, poor pedestrian crossings and slow emergency response contribute to road deaths.

title: Railway safety and reliability
description: Rail networks, including the new SGR, need reliable track, signalling, crossing and traction-power monitoring to prevent derailments and delays.

title: Vehicle theft, tracking and condition
description: Vehicle owners need protection against theft and early warning of faults such as low fuel, overheating and missed maintenance.

title: Parking, ticketing and passenger services
description: Parking, ferries, buses and airports suffer from queues, overloading, manual fare collection and poor passenger information.

title: Intrusion, theft and access control
description: Homes, server rooms, workshops and businesses need affordable ways to control access and detect intruders.

title: Examination cheating and identity fraud
description: Phones, impersonation and manual checks undermine fairness in examination halls.

title: Fire and hazardous gas leaks
description: LPG, chlorine dioxide and other gas leaks and electrical fires can cause deaths and destroy property if not detected early.

title: Safety and productivity in mining
description: Underground and small-scale miners face gas, collapse and flooding hazards and use inefficient processing methods.

title: Worker safety on sites
description: Construction, telecom and industrial workers face injuries when protective equipment is missing or hazards go unnoticed.

title: Comfort and automation in buildings
description: Air conditioning, ventilation, lighting, lifts and appliances are often manually controlled, which wastes energy and limits accessibility.

title: Affordable, clean cooking
description: Charcoal and firewood cooking harms health and forests. Electric, solar and induction cooking can be cleaner if they are affordable.

title: Solid waste collection and recycling
description: Overflowing bins, unsorted waste and limited recycling create health hazards and lose recoverable materials.

title: Air and noise pollution
description: Urban dust, vehicle emissions, kitchen fumes and noise affect health but are rarely measured locally.

title: Emergency response and early warning
description: Communities need early warning of floods and severe weather, and faster emergency response when accidents happen.

title: Automating industrial processes
description: Factories, ports and plants still rely on manual handling, inspection and dosing, which limits throughput, consistency and safety.

title: Hands-on training equipment for technical education
description: Technical institutions lack affordable laboratory kits, so students learn practical skills from theory alone.

title: Cashless payment and automated vending
description: Cash handling, queues and manual sales slow down retail, fuel and banking services.

title: Information, queues and services on campus
description: Libraries, registration, notices and voting on campus often depend on manual processes and paper.

title: Power and safety at telecom sites and data centres
description: Remote BTS towers and data centres depend on generators and batteries. Outages, fuel theft and unsafe maintenance raise costs.

title: Wildlife monitoring and conservation
description: Parks and guides need to know where wildlife is and protect it from conflict with people and infrastructure, using limited staff over large areas.

title: Controlling phone use where it is unsafe or disruptive
description: Phones cause cheating in exams, distraction while driving and security risks in banks. Detection, muting and jamming each raise different technical and legal questions.

title: Spoiled, adulterated or unsafe food and drink
description: Food and drink can spoil, be adulterated or vary in quality before it reaches people. Quick, affordable checks help sellers and buyers catch problems early.
